product_from_film: CrowdReply presents Searchmaxxing as a way to monitor and improve brand visibility in search and AI answers.
explains_well: Search, forum and video examples explain the idea of being visible wherever buyers look.
unclear: The dashboard shows where a brand loses visibility, but the action that wins it back is not shown.
scenario: A CRM search expands into many discovery channels, followed by a visibility dashboard and response table.
product_clear_basis: The dashboard at 34s shows visibility, citation and opportunity panels; the earlier montage explains the broad problem.

categories.finding: Search examples → being everywhere slogan → concept name → competitive threat → dashboard → score-check CTA.
An older search interface changes to a familiar best-CRM query, giving the opening a concrete discovery task.
The broad visibility problem is clear early; the monitoring product appears at 34s and serves brands concerned about discovery.
Search text, collage replacements, title states and dashboard/table changes are visible; exact rapid transition timing is unverified.
The search/forum/tutorial sequence shares a discovery theme; the later white state separates the status montage from the dashboard.
Crystalline blue/gold light and prismatic imagery make the concept reveal distinct from the cultural montage and flat UI.
Large slogans carry the argument. Dashboard labels and table rows get much less reading time.

categories.finding: Silent viewing conveys visibility competition and a score-check offer, but not the improvement workflow.
Large central text dominates the montage; red table rows focus attention on losses when the product appears.
Roughly the first 34s build the idea and threat; the dashboard and CTA occupy the final 13s.
The early search problem returns as visibility and ranking panels, but Win it back lacks a shown action/result.
Status imagery and competitive wording may create urgency or rivalry; audience response is unmeasured.
Discovery channels provide a shared theme; no single CRM query is clearly tracked through diagnosis and improvement.
Dashboard values and recovery wording are presented claims; actual visibility gains, data coverage and attribution are unverified.
Searchmaxxing language and the prismatic concept reveal give the film a strong identity; a clear recovery step would better distinguish the workflow.
Replace part of the competitive montage with one visible response problem and the exact action used to address it.
categories.experiment: Follow the opening CRM query into one highlighted response row, one suggested action and a later checked result.

categories.finding: For Tin, show where a campaign loses an audience and then the edit or distribution action that responds to it.
categories.experiment: Use one campaign title across a performance table, revised asset and updated channel preview.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

lessons.keep: Start with a familiar search query before expanding the visibility problem across channels.
try: Track the opening CRM query into one problem row, one corrective action and a checked result.
For Tin, carry one campaign title from performance table through asset revision to channel preview.
lessons.avoid: Using a recovery slogan as the only bridge between diagnosis and improvement.
lessons.open: The improvement action, data coverage, actual gains, asset provenance and audio remain unverified.

comparison.story: Search examples → everywhere slogan → named concept → competition → monitoring UI → score CTA.

comparison.lesson: A concrete opening query can anchor a broad visibility story if it is carried into the product demo.
